from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
    print(f'Page {i+1}: {len(t)} characters')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'PAGE {i+1}\\n'+p.read_text() for i,p in enumerate(sorted(Path('tmp/pdfs').glob('page-*.txt')))))
PY"

strengths: The mean-point correspondence provides a simple, original way to generate four-point pose hypotheses using established five-point and P3P solvers. Coupled with early refitting and refinement, this constitutes a useful practical contribution to a difficult geometric estimation problem and supports weak acceptance.

The experimental support is substantial: 90,000 camera triplets across 18 scenes and three datasets, two RANSAC frameworks, synthetic geometry/noise experiments, and component ablations. Supplementary evaluation using the maximum error across all three camera pairs strengthens the evidence beyond the main paper's averaged pose metric.

The results demonstrate useful accuracy–runtime improvements. In Table 3, 4p3v(A)+R+F+ENM achieves PhotoTourism AUC@10 of 76.56 at 32.37 ms, compared with 76.20 at 56.52 ms for the equivalently augmented five-point baseline. The mean-point variants also consistently improve aggregate accuracy over the homotopy baseline.

The manuscript clearly acknowledges the approximate nature of its solvers and tests the importance of refinement, filtering, and early non-minimal refitting. Hyperparameters are validated on a held-out scene, and archived code/data links plus implementation settings support reproducibility. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-2avk939s/call-2bd1dcd64c634a6ebcda99d0779be7e3/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: The runtime comparison with the homotopy solver is confounded by initialization. Section 8.3 reports approximately 45 ms to load weights/data once per RANSAC run, while Table 3 reports total homotopy runtimes around 60–67 ms. Separating initialization from execution with cached weights is necessary to establish how much of the reported speed advantage comes from estimation itself. This concern does not invalidate the accuracy improvements.

The strongest speed–accuracy claims exceed the comparisons provided. Although Tables 2–3 include the fully augmented five-point baseline, Figure 4's runtime curves and Table 7's GC-RANSAC comparison omit that baseline. Moreover, the most accurate proposed variant achieves PhotoTourism AUC@10 of 77.14 versus 76.20 for the augmented baseline, but costs 112.60 versus 56.52 ms. Its additional accuracy therefore carries a substantial computational cost.

The claim that scene dependence becomes negligible after ENM is insufficiently supported. Lemma 1 bounds the virtual correspondence's image-space error by triangle size; it provides no corresponding pose-error or convergence guarantee. Figure 9 shows residual approximation error even without image noise, and Figure 15 includes configurations such as Old Hospital where the five-point baseline achieves higher accuracy at larger budgets. These observations warrant narrower robustness claims.

A correctable reporting concern appears in Table 7: for Cambridge Landmarks, the 4p3v(M)+R+F and 4p3v(M)+R+F+ENM rows exactly repeat the corresponding affine-method rows across every reported metric, including runtime. These entries need verification because they affect interpretation of the component ablations.
